2026-11-12.title: Thursday of the Thirty-second Week in Ordinary Time · St Josaphat, Bishop and Martyr
readings: No longer as a slave but as a beloved brother
Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob
The kingdom of God is among you
2026-11-12.alt: Memorial of St Josaphat, bishop and martyr.
2026-11-12.verse: For, in fact, the kingdom of God is among you.
theo: The Pharisees want signs and dates: when will the Kingdom come? Jesus answers that it is “not coming with things that can be observed”, because it is already “among you”, present in his own person. Before the final day of the Son of Man, he must “endure much suffering and be rejected by this generation”. The Kingdom comes through the Cross.

Philemon, the shortest of Paul's letters, shows the Kingdom at work in a household. Onesimus, a runaway slave, has become a Christian through Paul in prison. Paul sends him back, asking Philemon to receive him “no longer as a slave but more than a slave, a beloved brother”. Without a single slogan, the Gospel plants the seed that will undo slavery. St Josaphat, a Ukrainian bishop martyred in 1623, gave his life for the unity of Eastern Christians with Rome: the Kingdom among us is a communion of brothers.
outline: Ask: where would you look for signs of God's Kingdom today?

“The kingdom of God is among you.”
live: Treat someone who serves you (a driver, a helper) as a brother or sister today.
Pray for Christian unity and for the Eastern Catholic Churches.
2026-11-12.prayer: Lord Jesus, your Kingdom is among us. Open my eyes to see it, my heart to receive every person as a brother or sister, and give your Church the unity for which St Josaphat gave his life. Amen.

quick: The Kingdom is already among us in Christ.
The Gospel turns slaves into brothers.
2026-11-12.action: Treat someone who serves you as a brother or sister.
2026-11-12.question: Whom do I treat as less than a brother?

homily: Dear friends, the Pharisees wanted signs and dates: when will the Kingdom come? Jesus answered that the Kingdom of God is not coming with things that can be observed; it is already among you (Luke 17:20–21). It is present in his own person.

And he adds a hard word: before the day of the Son of Man, he must endure much suffering and be rejected by this generation (Luke 17:25). The Kingdom does not come through power and spectacle; it comes through the Cross.

The short letter to Philemon shows the Kingdom at work in a household. Paul sends back a runaway slave, Onesimus, who has become a Christian, and asks Philemon to receive him no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother (Philemon 16). The Gospel quietly changes the most ordinary relationships.

Today we honour St Josaphat, who gave his life for the unity of Christians. The Kingdom is among us when walls come down: between master and servant, between Churches, between neighbours. Treat someone today who serves you as a brother or sister. Amen.
kids: Children, God's Kingdom is wherever people love one another like brothers and sisters. Be kind today to someone who helps you: a driver, a cleaner, a cook.

intro: The Kingdom is present in Christ, transforms our relationships, and builds unity.

q: And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed, nor shall this kingdom be left to another people. It shall crush all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, and it shall stand forever.

Once Jesus was asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God was coming, and he answered, “The kingdom of God is not coming with things that can be observed; nor will they say, ‘Look, here it is!’ or ‘There it is!’ For, in fact, the kingdom of God is among you.”
points.apply: Look today for one quiet sign of God's Kingdom.

sub: The Gospel changes how we see people.
Family is defined by doing God's will.
q: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Come closer to me.” And they came closer. He said, “I am your brother, Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.”
For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
points.apply: Treat someone who serves you as family.

sub: Josaphat worked for unity with Rome.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
That they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.

concl: The Kingdom grows among brothers and sisters.
